ALPHABET CENTER · LETTER O

Letter O — Orange.

A round orange rolls in for the letter O. O is itself a perfect circle — and the orange is the roundest, friendliest word it could wear.

Meet the letter, hear its sound, trace it together — then play. Everything on this page is free, gentle and paced for you.

THE LETTER SOUND

What does O say?

“o — oh, a round open sound”

O says oh — a round, open sound you make with a big circle mouth. Like an orange! Say ohhh while opening your mouth wider and wider.

TRACE THE LETTER

Trace O o together.

Follow the numbers with a finger — on screen or on each other’s palms. The arrows show the way to go, the numbers show where to start, and a grown-up reads the little script below each card. Slow and wobbly is exactly right.

Trace the uppercase O

One stroke. Start at 1 at the top right, sweep anticlockwise — up, round to the left, down and round the bottom — all the way back to where you began.

Trace the lowercase o

One stroke. Start at 1 at the right side, sweep anticlockwise — over the top, round the left, along the bottom — all the way back.

TAKE IT OFF SCREEN

Orange roll.

Two minutes is plenty. Follow your child’s lead and stop while it is still fun — that is the whole method.

  1. 01

    Roll an orange (or a ball) across the table to each other, saying ohhh with every roll.

  2. 02

    Peel it together and breathe in the smell — that scent is the lesson sticking.

  3. 03

    Share the segments and count them: oh, oh, oh — one, two, three.

PLAY & PRACTICE

Games that use this letter.

The games mix every letter — play them after meeting two or three letters, or any day your child asks. No scores, no timers, no wrong answers that count.
